nodes.name: Ni(OH)2 Hydrothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.34 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O was dissolved with 12 mL methanol and 0.85 mL DMF. Then, the mixed solution was transferred to 25 mL of clean Teflon-lined autoclave with a clean Ni foam (2×2.5 cm²) after ultrasonic homogenization. It was placed at 151.5°C for 550 min. After the reaction was completed, the green material was clamped and rinsed with deionized water (DW) and ethanol. It was dried under vacuum at 40°C for standby. The result catalyst is named as Ni(OH)2.

nodes.name: Ni3S2 Hydrothermal Vulcanization
nodes.procedure: 0.34 mmol Na2S·9H2O was dissolved in 12 mL DW by using ultrasonic dispersion. Then, the solution was mixed with Ni(OH)2 nanosheet in 25 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. After heating at 100°C for 480 min, the catalyst was cooled to room temperature and washed with DW and ethanol. Then the back material was transferred to 40°C vacuum to dry. The final catalyst is named Ni3S2.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM confirms integrity of two-dimensional nanosheet structure for Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 and Pt_{1+n}/NiS_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S6, SEM and TEM images could further confirm the integrity of the two-dimensional nanosheet structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM confirms two-dimensional nanosheet structure and integrity for Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 and Pt_{1+n}/NiS_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S6, SEM and TEM images could further confirm the integrity of the two-dimensional nanosheet structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacing of 0.235 nm and 0.200 nm corresponding to Ni_3S_2 (021) and NiS_2 (220) crystal planes respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the lattice spacing of 0.235 and 0.200 nm should correspond to Ni_3S_2 (021) and NiS_2 (220) crystal planes detected by high-resolution TEM (HRTEM), respectively (Fig. S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED confirms existence of (021), (104), and (110) crystal planes of Ni_3S_2 in Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) clearly confirms the existence of (0 2 1), (1 0 4), and (1 1 0) crystal planes of Ni_3S_2, respectively (Fig. 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM reveals coexistence of Pt single atoms and sub-nanoclusters nearby nickel atoms in Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 and Pt_{1+n}/NiS_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) revealed the coexistence of Pt SAs and NCs nearby nickel atoms (Fig. 1b and c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mapping shows Pt, Ni, O, S uniformly distributed on Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the element mapping and element composition diagram of Pt_{1 + n} / Ni_3S_2 reveal that Pt, Ni, O and S elements are uniformly distributed on the substrate (Fig. 1d and Fig. S7b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt loading determined as 5.18 wt% for Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 and 6.74 wt% for Pt_{1+n}/NiS_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The loading of Pt was determined to be 5.18 and 6.74 wt% by the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES), respectively (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows characteristic peaks of Ni_3S_2 and NiS_2 with no obvious Pt nanoparticle peaks, indicating Pt single atoms and sub-nanoclusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown as XRD analysis (Fig. 2a), those obvious characteristic peaks about Ni_3S_2 are detected. More importantly, no obvious peak about Pt nanoparticle is detected.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Pt 4f_{7/2} at 70.6 eV and 4f_{5/2} at 73.4 eV for Pt^0; Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 shows higher oxidation state Pt peaks at 72.3 and 75.5 eV; Ni 2p peaks shift indicating electron transfer from Ni to Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the orbits of Pt 4f_{7 / 2} and Pt 4f_{5 / 2} at 70.6 and 73.4 eV are attributed to Pt^0. For Pt_{1 + n} / Ni_3S_2, the fitting peaks at 72.3 and 75.5 eV should be attributed to the higher oxidation state of Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES shows average Pt valence states of +1.1 for Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 and +0.6 for Pt_{1+n}/NiS_2; FT-EXAFS shows Pt-O at 1.75 Å for Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 and Pt-S at 1.98 Å for Pt_{1+n}/NiS_2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the average valence states of Pt atoms are +1.1 and +0.6 for Pt_{1 + n} / Ni_3S_2 and Pt_{1 + n} / NiS_2 respectively. The FT-EXAFS curves of Pt_{1 + n} / Ni_3S_2 show obvious coordination peak at 1.75 Å, which should be attributed to Pt-O bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: Quantitative EXAFS fitting shows Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 has Pt-O and Pt-Ni coordination numbers of 1 at 1.97 Å and 2.54 Å; Pt_{1+n}/NiS_2 has Pt-S and Pt-Ni coordination numbers of 2 at 2.60 Å and 2.65 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is confirmed that Pt_{1 + n} / Ni_3S_2 has satisfied Pt-O first shell coordination and Pt-Ni second shell coordination, and the coordination numbers of Pt-O and Pt-Ni both are 1 with the bonding distances of 1.97 Å and 2.54 Å, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows weak δ_{Pt-OH} peaks at 1062 cm^{-1} and H-O-H bending at 1630 cm^{-1} for Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2, indicating Pt-O bonds from Pt-OH facilitate Volmer step.
nodes.evidence_snippet: weak δ_{Pt - OH} peaks are detected on the surface of Pt_{1 + n}/ Ni_3S_2 ADCs at 1062 cm^{-1} and no obvious change. Obviously, the H-O-H bending vibration peak at 1630 cm^{-1} shows that Pt_{1 + n} / Ni_3S_2 ADCs are conducive to Volmer step.

nodes.characterization_summary: ATR-SEIRAS shows significant red shift in peaks between 1600 cm^{-1} and 3000-3600 cm^{-1} for Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2, indicating strong H_2O adsorption and easy O-H bond breaking.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peaks of Pt_{1 + n} / Ni_3S_2 ADCs between 1600 cm^{-1} and 3000 - 3600 cm^{-1} show significant red shift, indicating that the Pt - O_1Ni_1 active sites could generate strong adsorption effect on *H_2O and break the O-H bond more easily.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV shows double layer capacitance C_dl of 50.66 mF cm^{-2} for Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2, indicating largest ECSA among samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt_{1 + n} / Ni_3S_2 shows the largest C_dl value of 50.66 mF cm^{-2} among samples, which is close to Pt / C (49.46 mF cm^{-2}) but much higher than Pt_{1 + n} / NiS_2 (25.78 mF cm^{-2})

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance R_ct of 1.3 Ω for Pt_{1+n}/Ni_3S_2 under 10 mA cm^{-2}, smaller than Pt/C (1.4 Ω).
